race_context: Greenwood Community School Corporation serves the city of Greenwood in Johnson County; Dr. Terry Terhune is superintendent {gcsc_min0925}. A current enrollment figure could not be confirmed from a fetched source.

Board: at the Sept. 16, 2025 meeting, Chad Shaffer presided as board president, with Peggy Daeger, Jack Napier and Lori Feller present and Sheila Martin listed as the board's Central Nine Career Center representative {gcsc_min0925}. The board's size, its district/at-large structure and current officers could not be confirmed on a fetched district page, because the district website blocks automated access.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows District 2 (vote for 1), with Napier as the only candidate, and an at-large race (vote for 1) with Shaffer, Laura Chisholm and Feller {in_list}. Napier, Shaffer and Feller are current board members {gcsc_min0925}; BallotReady also lists Feller as a current at-large member {br_feller}.

Seat count: whether the at-large race fills one seat or two could not be confirmed from a fetched source. Daily Journal coverage that could not be read (see gaps) indicates that two at-large seats were filled in 2022, which would put two at-large seats on the 2026 ballot.
Party labels: on the state list, Shaffer and Feller are Republican, and Napier and Chisholm are Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Budget and finances: at the Sept. 16, 2025 meeting, the chief financial officer held public hearings on the 2026 budget and the bus and capital plans. She told the board that incoming student transfers account for about $5.5 million in revenue and are one reason the district has kept its financial footing {gcsc_min0925}. That meeting also approved higher substitute-teacher pricing to stay competitive with neighboring districts {gcsc_min0925}.

Other 2025 actions: the board approved the 2026–27 calendar, which was aligned with Central Nine Career Center's, and renewed its agreement with Adult and Child Services as school-based provider, which serves about 7% of students. The technology director reported that a Verkada building-security system was in place {gcsc_min0925}.
Forums: no 2026 Greenwood candidate forum, questionnaire or candidate website could be read. The Daily Journal, the main local paper, blocks automated access.
